fear.name: Despair
fear.hint: The Despair pool of the GM.

forcePrivateRolls.name: Force private player rolls
forcePrivateRolls.hint: Every player roll is whispered to that player and the GMs. Nobody sees anyone else's dice.

enforceAnonymity.name: Keep character sheets anonymous
enforceAnonymity.hint: Holds default ownership at None, so no player can open another player's sheet. Each player still owns their own.

searchTokensPerRoom.name: Search tokens per room
searchTokensPerRoom.hint: How many times one room can be searched in a single time of day.

lockRollDialog.name: Lock the roll window for players
lockRollDialog.hint: Players cannot touch the dice, the statistic, advantage, experiences or the situational bonus. Those come from the action, a Hope Call or the GM. Picking an experience no longer charges Hope quietly either — spending it is the Experience Hope Call. GMs are unaffected.

roomVisibility.name: Players only see who is in their room
roomVisibility.hint: Hides other characters unless they stand in the same room. Walls and vision get most of the way there; this closes the gaps left by doorways, archways and maps built without walls. GMs see everything.

lockPlayerResources.name: Players cannot edit Actions, Hope or statistics
lockPlayerResources.hint: Those move through play — spend an action, take a rest, earn a Level Up. HP and Stress stay editable: players mark their own damage. GMs are unaffected.

chargeMovement.name: Crossing rooms costs a Move
chargeMovement.hint: Moving inside a room is free. Crossing into another Scene Region spends the free Move for that time of day, then an action. Turn off to handle movement by hand.

despairFromRolls.name: Rolls grant Despair
despairFromRolls.hint: A roll that lands with Despair feeds the pool of that student's Monokuma. Divide the students up from the gear on the Despair bar.

hideSystemFear.name: Replace the Daggerheart Fear tracker
hideSystemFear.hint: Hides Daggerheart's single shared Fear bar and gives every Monokuma a Despair pool of their own. Turn off to go back to the system tracker.

pixelFont.name: Pixel font
pixelFont.hint: Press Start 2P on interface chrome: HUD, Despair, character name, statistic labels, tabs. Journals, chat and editable fields keep the normal face so long text stays readable.

debug.name: Verbose console logging
debug.hint: Print Danganronpa RPG diagnostics to the browser console. This client only.

musicEnabled.name: Music follows the game state
musicEnabled.hint: Swaps the playlist when the Eclipse opens, a Class Trial or Investigation begins, the time of day turns, or the game goes on hold. Map the playlists first: GM panel → Right now → Music by state. A murder incident never changes the music.

voiceEnabled.name: Regional voice (needs LiveKit AVClient)
voiceEnabled.hint: Every mapped room becomes its own LiveKit channel — you hear only whoever stands in the room with you. Needs avclient-livekit installed, active and pointed at a working server. Off by default.

SearchTokens.title: Search Tokens
SearchTokens.allFull: Every room still holds all {max} tokens.
SearchTokens.exhausted: This room is searched out. Try again next time of day.
SearchTokens.pickedClean: Somebody got here first. The action is spent.
SearchTokens.noGm: No GM is connected, so no search token can be spent.
SearchTokens.timeout: No GM answered. The search was not counted.

Sheet.ultimatePlaceholder: the one thing this character does best

Guard.blocked: Only the GM changes that. Actions, Hope and statistics move through play.

Listen.prompt: You are in {room}. Which neighbouring room?
Listen.anonymous: {n} person(s) in {room}. You cannot tell who.
Listen.critical: You catch it all at once:

Actions.label: Actions
Actions.pipTooltip: Set remaining actions to {n}. Click the last filled one to spend it.
Actions.woundedTooltip: All HP is marked — one action per time of day.
Actions.lockedTooltip: Forfeit. All HP is marked, so this stays shut until they heal.
Actions.pipReadOnly: {left} of {max} actions this time of day. Spent by acting.
Actions.freeMoveAvailable: Free Move still available this time of day.
Actions.freeMoveSpent: Free Move used. The next crossing costs an action.
Actions.allSpent: No actions left. They come back when the next Eclipse begins.

Assign.title: Whose Despair feeds which Monokuma
Assign.intro: A roll that lands with Despair feeds that student's Monokuma.
Assign.failed: The division could not be saved. See the console.
Assign.noMonokumas: Assistant GMs do not get a Despair pool.
Assign.implicitHint: Never assigned — falling back to the first Monokuma.
Assign.footnote: * = unassigned, using the fallback. Choose “— nobody —” to keep a student out of every pool: a Mastermind, an NPC, a template.

Despair.label: Despair
Despair.pipTooltip: Set {name}'s Despair to {n}. Click the last filled one to spend it.
Despair.notEnoughPool: That pool holds {held} Despair; {needed} was asked for.
Despair.hopeAlreadyFull: Their Hope is already at maximum.
Despair.hopeConverted: {who} converts some of their Despair — you gain {n} Hope.
Despair.poolsIntro: Name each pool. It need not match the account.
Despair.noCandidates: No Assistant GM to grant a pool to. Full Gamemasters have one already.

Hud.advance: Next time of day — refills actions, free Moves and search tokens
Hud.startEclipse: Start the Eclipse — lights out, everyone places their token (2 crossings)
Hud.endEclipse: End the Eclipse and begin the next time of day
Hud.rewind: Step back one time of day. A correction — it refills nothing
Hud.elapsedTooltip: How long this time of day has run. It turns amber at 15 minutes and red at 30 — the handbook's advice is one action by the first mark and both by the second.
Hud.freeMovesLeftTooltip: Students who still have their free Move.
Hud.startEclipseNamed: Start the {time} Eclipse — lights out, everyone places their token (2 crossings)
Hud.startEclipseFree: Start the {time} Eclipse — lights out, everyone picks any room on the map
Hud.startEclipseNewSession: End the session and open the {time} Eclipse — a new session, and everyone places their token (2 crossings)
Hud.eclipseRunningTooltip: The placement window before this time of day. It has not begun yet — the clock moves when the Eclipse ends.

Action.failed: That action could not be completed. See the console.
Action.traitOnlyIfOpen: Used only if the project above demands nothing of its own.
Action.cannotAfford: You have {left} action(s) left and this needs {needed}.
Action.costMove: free once per time of day
Action.noRoom: Your token is outside every room. Move it into one, or ask the GM.
Action.tokensLeft: {room}: {n} search token(s) left this time of day.
Action.moveFree: Used the free Move for this time of day.
Action.movePaid: No free Move left, so this one cost an action.
Action.observeCrit: Critical — a Truth Bullet with its category identified, and a substantial hint from the GM.
Action.observeGm: Total {total}. Score it against the Observe table for whatever they are looking at. A failure costs them 2 Stress.
Action.searchGoalHint: What turns up depends on the room and the roll.
Action.goalCrimeHint: A potential murder tool. Leaves a Prep Remnant.
Action.goalCleaningHint: A cleaning tool. Leaves a Prep Remnant.
Action.goalSpecificHint: Describe it. The GM rules on what was really there.
Action.goalSpecificPlaceholder: e.g. anything belonging to the victim
Action.goalSpecificNeeded: Describe what you are looking for first.
Action.specificFound: The roll reached Tier {tier}. Decide what was there.
Action.specificNothing: The roll found nothing. Say so, or offer something lesser.
Action.specificSent: Your description is with the GM. They will say what you found.
Action.dynamicHint: Describe what you are doing; the GM sets the difficulty. Dynamic actions have gentler thresholds than the standard ones — that is the reward for inventing something.
Action.dynamicDescribe: Describe what your character does. The GM reads this and sets the difficulty.
Action.dynamicPlaceholder: e.g. I water the plants in the garden, looking for anything buried.
Action.dynamicSetBy: Now set the difficulty and the statistic:
Action.dynamicNoRuling: No GM answered. The attempt is off and nothing was spent.
Action.dynamicDescription: Any action at all, provided you describe it in detail — the GM sets the difficulty and the statistic. The thresholds are gentler than the standard actions, as a deliberate reward for inventing something.
Action.noRoomNote: Your token is outside every room.
Action.callsGmNote: The GM judges this one. Your roll and your request go to them.
Action.gmPrompt: {action} — what are you trying to do? The GM sees this with your roll.

placeholder.think: e.g. Who could have got into the pool room unseen?
placeholder.listen: e.g. Listening at the door to the kitchen.
placeholder.analyze: e.g. Analysing the torn cloth from the hallway.
placeholder.observe: e.g. Looking for anything around the body.
placeholder.directMurder: Who, where and how — as agreed beforehand.

Action.analyzeGm: Score this against the Analyze table for that Truth Bullet. A failure locks it for them until the chapter ends.
Action.murderConfirm: This opens a direct murder. It needs prior agreement with the GM and the consent of the other player. The action is spent even if the conditions fail.
Action.murderPrompt: Confirm the plan for the GM: the victim, the room, and anything you are relying on.
Action.murderPromptVictim: You are alone with {victim}. Confirm the plan for the GM: how you are doing it, and anything you are relying on.
Action.murderNobody: Nobody here to kill. The attempt is spent; try again another time of day.
Action.murderWitness: You are not alone with your victim — {n} other person(s) would see it. The attempt is spent; try again another time of day.
Action.murderBlocked: The conditions were not met. Nothing happened, and the action is spent.
Action.sabotageSeen: {actor} is seen doing something to a project in {room}.
Action.sabotageWatched: {actor} is doing something to {project} in {room}, and everyone here can see roughly what.
Action.sabotageCarryOn: Carry on anyway? Nothing is spent yet.

Analyze.askHint: Ask the GM for a hint
Analyze.noBullets: You have nothing left to analyse.
Analyze.sent: The GM is working out what {name} really is.
Analyze.failed: You cannot make sense of {name}. It stays with you, still Neutral, and you cannot try this one again until the next chapter.
Analyze.critPrompt: {actor} identified {name} as a {type} on a critical — they have earned a substantial hint on top of it.

Items.title: Items — {actor}
Items.name: Name
Items.namePlaceholder: Type anything, or pick a suggestion
Items.descriptionPlaceholder: What it is, or what it tells them.
Items.overCapNote: A GM grant ignores the carry limit. Going over is allowed and will be flagged.
Items.lost: {item} is no longer in your inventory.
Items.failed: That did not work. See the console.
Items.usePrompt: What are you using it for?
Items.useConsumes: The item is used up either way.
Items.usedNothing: Nothing to restore. You were already whole.
Items.useStashed: That is in your stash. Take it out first.
Items.equipStashed: That is in your stash. Take it out before holding it ready.
Items.noneReadied: Nothing is held ready — only what is in your hand counts in an incident or a clean-up.
Items.creativePrompt: {item} is Tier 0: a random, seemingly useless item. Tell the GM what you are doing with it.
Items.creativePlaceholder: e.g. jam the stapler into the door latch so it cannot close
Items.creativeSent: Sent to the GM. The item stays with you until they rule on it.
Items.wouldRestoreNothing: It restores nothing — you are already full on everything it gives.

Monocub.hopeReadout: Hope: {held} / {max}. Only a GM tops this up.
Monocub.cannotMeddle: Not enough action, or not enough Hope.
Monocub.mustBeDead: Only a character who has already died becomes a Monocub.
Monocub.opted: {name} has joined the GMs as a Monocub.
Monocub.dialogIntro: A dead player may join the GMs as a Monocub once their own trial has ended. Tick to opt them in — the timing is your judgement, not the module's.
Monocub.giveHope: Turn a Monokuma's Despair into Hope
Monocub.silencedNote: Tick if this Monocub stumbled onto the crime scene. They cannot discuss it until the chapter ends, but Confusion still works on the incident's crisis actions.
Monocub.needHope: Confusion costs Hope and you have none. Ask a GM to convert some Despair.
Monocub.nobodyHere: Nobody in this room to use Confusion on.
Monocub.meddleIntro: Nudge somebody's next roll from the sidelines. They will not know it was you.
Monocub.silencedNoteShort: You stumbled onto the crime. No discussing it until next chapter.
Monocub.noneYet: Nobody has opted in as a Monocub yet.
Monocub.silenceOn: You stumbled onto the crime. You may not discuss it until this chapter ends.
Monocub.silenceOff: The silence is lifted. You may discuss the crime again.

Mastermind.privacyWarning: This screen names the Mastermind. Do not share your view while it is open.
Mastermind.dialogIntro: Picked before the season, with the player's agreement. Despair converts into their Hope 1:1 — the same trade a Monocub gets.
Mastermind.noneSet: No Mastermind set. Pick one from the GM panel first.
Mastermind.toggleFinalTrial: Start or end the Final Trial
Mastermind.confirmStart: Announce the Final Trial? This is public — everyone sees it start.
Mastermind.confirmEnd: Clear the Final Trial flag? Nothing already applied is undone.
Mastermind.ended: The Final Trial flag is cleared.
Mastermind.finalTruthPlaced: A Final Truth Remnant has already been placed this chapter.
Mastermind.finalTruthReminder: No Final Truth Remnant this chapter yet. One a chapter, pointing at the Mastermind — drop it with the ordinary Remnant tools, type “Final Truth Remnant”.
Mastermind.verdictIntro: Only you know whether the vote named the Mastermind. Say who was accused and pick the outcome.
Mastermind.alreadyDeadNote: The Mastermind died earlier this season. The same rule applies whoever was accused: reveal the truth, execute nobody new.
Mastermind.verdictNote: Correct: the Mastermind is executed and the killing game is over. Wrong, or already dead: nobody new is executed — the table is shown that the game was never what it looked like.
Mastermind.revealedText: The game they were playing was never what it seemed.

Floor.nobody: There is nobody alive to give the floor to.
Floor.startIntro: A volunteer opens, then the floor passes down the order. Three minutes each, uninterrupted — unless somebody objects.
Floor.startNote: The order is everyone still alive, from the volunteer. An OBJECTION takes the floor from whoever holds it.
Floor.startTrialIntro: Everything the trial needs, in one step. Choose who opens and this does the rest.
Floor.startTrialStepPhase: The campaign moves to Class Trial.
Floor.startTrialStepFloor: The floor opens and the speaking order is built from the living.
Floor.startTrialStepAnnounce: The trial is announced in chat and the music follows.
Floor.trialOpened: The Class Trial is in session. {who} opens.
Floor.endTrialConfirm: This closes the floor and opens the vote. The verdict comes after it.
Floor.objectionNote: You never move the floor for an objection: presenting evidence takes it.
Floor.evidenceHint: Truth Bullets presented in this trial.

Vote.openIntro: Send every player a ballot, then count them. Both halves are this button.
Vote.privacyNote: Ballots never touch world data. They go to the GMs, are counted in memory and are not kept. The results are published; the votes are not.
Vote.opened: {n} ballots are out. Name who you believe is the Blackened.
Vote.noVoters: No player is connected with a character to vote.
Vote.ballotIntro: Vote for whoever you believe is the Blackened. You may vote for yourself, for Monokuma, and for the dead.
Vote.ballotNote: Nobody sees who you voted for. Only the totals are published.
Vote.dismissed: Ballot closed without a vote. Nothing was counted for you — ask the GM to send it again.
Vote.notRunning: No vote is open right now.
Vote.tied: A tie. That is a loss for the students.
Vote.verdictIntro: Only you know whether they got it right. Name who is executed and who the Blackened really was, then pick the outcome.
Vote.verdictNote: Right: the Blackened is executed and every survivor takes a Level Up. Wrong — a tie counts as wrong — the accused is executed, the Blackened stays anonymous and in play with a Reinforced Level Up and one new rule of their choosing, and every Monokuma fills their Despair.
Vote.wrongSummary: The students named the wrong person.
Vote.blackenedRewarded: The Blackened stays anonymous and in play, and takes a {kind} Level Up.
Vote.newRule: The Blackened introduces one new rule of their choosing, with Monokuma's consent.
Vote.twoBlackened: This chapter produced {n} Blackened. Name all of them — half an answer is not one.

Music.title: Music by state
Music.intro: Pick which playlist plays when. The module never starts a playlist you have not chosen here, and ships no audio of its own.
Music.orderNote: The first state that applies wins, in the order listed. A Class Trial at night uses the trial's playlist; an Eclipse during one uses the Eclipse's.
Music.incidentNote: A murder incident has no entry on purpose. A track that only ever played during one would tell the whole table a murder is happening. Whatever is playing keeps playing.
Music.fadeNote: Fades are the playlist's own — set Fade Duration on the playlist or on a track, and both directions use it. Play a track by hand and the state's playlist pauses where it stands, then resumes from there.
Music.noPlaylists: This world has no playlists. Make one in the Playlists sidebar first.

Casebook.title: {actor} — what you know
Casebook.buttonTooltip: Your evidence, grouped by where you found it. The badge counts what is still worth analysing.
Casebook.empty: No Truth Bullets yet. Observe a room to start finding them.
Casebook.lockedNote: {n} of them failed an Analyze this chapter. Those copies stay unidentified until the next chapter begins — somebody else's copy of the same trace is not locked.
Casebook.noRoom: Where it came from was never recorded
Casebook.launcherTooltip: Your Truth Bullets — open during the Class Trial

Cleanup.title: Cleaning up
Cleanup.hint: Spend 1 Stress to erase one trace you left. A readied Cleaning Tool makes it easier. Reinforced traces do not come off.
Cleanup.intro: Pick a trace. Each attempt costs {n} Stress and is not an action.
Cleanup.withTool: {item} (Tier {tier}) in hand — advantage, and that much off the threshold.
Cleanup.noneReadied: No Cleaning Tool readied. Hold one ready on the Inventory tab first.
Cleanup.notYours: You are not the one cleaning up this scene.
Cleanup.nothingHere: Nothing to clean up in this room.
Cleanup.allReinforced: Every trace here is reinforced. None of it comes off.
Cleanup.rerollLost: A Reroll arrived for a clean-up this browser has no record of — a reload, or another GM took over. The dice are already rewritten, so score the new number against the same trace by hand: put the Remnant back if the first attempt erased it, remove anything the botched wipe left, and refund the Stress.
Cleanup.reinforced: The {what} will not come off. Whatever left it, left it for good.
Cleanup.vanished: The trace you were working on is already gone. The effort still cost you.
Cleanup.leftTrace: Your cleaning left a trace of its own ({visibility}).

band.despair: Gone — but you were not careful about it.
band.failure: It will not come off, and you made a mess trying.

Cleanup.gmTool: Readied: {item} (Tier {tier}) — advantage, and {tier} off every threshold below.
Cleanup.gmNoTool: No Cleaning Tool readied — bare hands, no advantage.
Cleanup.gmNothingHere: No traces in the room the killer is standing in.
Cleanup.gmAttemptsLeft: Stress left for {n} more attempt(s). Stage 6 ends when that runs out, or when you close the murder — closing destroys the tools that were used.
Cleanup.trailPlanted: Planted a Prep Remnant ({visibility}) pointing at {name}.
Cleanup.bodyMoved: The body has been moved to {room}.
Cleanup.bodyStuck: There is nowhere to take it.
Cleanup.noBody: There is no body here to move.
Cleanup.bodyNote: {name}'s body was dragged out of here towards {room}.
Cleanup.seenCleaning: {actor} is doing something in {room}, and not hiding it well.

Murder.openIntro: One opening roll, then a turn-based incident. A direct murder opens on the killer's roll; a trap opens on the victim's.
Murder.indirect: Indirect murder — the victim is alone, and the drain is doubled
Murder.sameActor: The killer and the victim cannot be the same person.
Murder.needTwo: There must be at least two living students.
Murder.opened: {killer} is moving on {victim}. Throw the opening roll.
Murder.dayNote: Not night, so the opening roll is unmodified.
Murder.keyCount: This case will leave {n} Key Remnants.
Murder.ranOut: {name} is out of HP and out of Stress. The incident ends and they are dead — no Finishing Blow was needed, and none was earned.
Murder.rerollLost: A Reroll arrived for a crisis action this incident has no record of — another action has happened since, or it was somebody else's roll. Nothing was replayed, so the FIRST result stands and the dice on the player's screen no longer match it. Score the new number by hand, or have them take the action again.
Murder.nobodyElse: There is nobody else alive to walk in.
Murder.endConfirm: Close this murder? The incident state is cleared. Nothing already applied is undone.
Murder.afterTitle: The incident is over — what now
Murder.afterIntro: {killer} against {victim}. Everything below follows from what just happened, and the module has stopped tracking the incident itself.
Murder.afterNoRoom: The victim's token is outside every room. Put it where the body is before announcing it.
Murder.afterAutopsy: The autopsy Truth Bullet has not been issued.
Murder.afterDirect: A direct murder — whoever was in the room saw it happen.
Murder.afterIndirect: A trap — nobody saw it, and setting it left traces of its own.
Murder.actionBlocked: They have shut this one down for now.
Murder.actionHindered: They have made this harder — you roll at disadvantage.
Murder.noStressLeft: Resolution actions cost Stress, and you have none.
Murder.killerChooses: Critical — the killer chooses: 2 HP, 2 Stress, or 1 of each.
Murder.hinderedActions: {n} of their action(s) at disadvantage for {turns} turns.
Murder.blockedActions: {n} of their action(s) shut down entirely for {turns} turns.
Murder.rolesSwapped: The roles are reversed. The killer is the one bleeding now.
Murder.victimDead: The victim is dead. The killer is Blackened.
Murder.resolutionNote: Stage 6. The killer now sees the Remnants on the map and can use resolution actions. Reinforced traces stay put. A crime tool that was used is destroyed.
Murder.thirdIntro: One free choice: get them out with you, take a side, or turn away.
Murder.actionSpent: You have already taken that one this incident.
Murder.drainStopped: The bleeding stops — no further HP or Stress is lost this incident.
Murder.indirectBegins: The trap closes. The incident begins with the victim alone, losing 2 a turn.
Murder.tierZeroIntro: {actor} is swinging {item}, a Tier 0 object. A Tier 0 item may count as Tier 1 or 2 when the killer is being creative — how good is this use?
Murder.tierZeroNote: Tier 0 deals 1 damage, Tier 1 deals 2, Tier 2 deals 2 and 3 on a critical. Dismissing this leaves it at Tier 0.
Murder.improvised: Snatched a weapon out of the struggle: {item} (Tier {tier}).
Murder.improvisedNote: Grabbed mid-incident. A crime tool like any other.
Murder.cannotLeave: You are in an incident. The only way out is a crisis action.
Murder.actionsLocked: You are in an incident. Use your crisis actions; Hope Calls still work.
Murder.thirdJoined: {name} throws in with the killer and stays in the incident.
Murder.thirdLeft: {name} turns away and leaves. They take no part in this.
Murder.openingYours: This roll is yours, and it is the only one. It cannot be skipped.
Murder.openingRequired: This roll cannot be skipped. Throw it.
Murder.openingDeclined: {name} did not throw the opening roll. Stage 4 is still open; press the button again when they are ready.
Murder.openingRemnantNote: {name} sensed the attempt ({band}). Something of the struggle was left to notice.
Murder.leftRemnants: Leaves {n} traces ({visibility}), and the killer cannot wipe them.
Murder.keyRemnantsStale: The roles reversed, so the case changed: the five Key Remnants were planned around a killer who is now the victim. Plan a new set before the Investigation.
Murder.nightNoteDirect: It is night: the killer's opening roll has advantage.
Murder.nightNoteIndirect: It is night: the victim's opening roll has disadvantage.

Investigation.plannerIntro: Five clues for chapter {chapter}. Together they should narrow the suspects to {min}–{max} people.
Investigation.plannerNote: The floor is {min} reachable clues. Below that the case may not be solvable.
Investigation.tokenGone: Its Remnant is gone from the map
Investigation.tooThin: Only {found} Key Remnants have been found. The floor is {min} — below that the trial has no honest answer. Point the players at what is left, or let it stand and pay for it at the vote.
Investigation.createNote: Pick a room on any row not already on the map. Apply places that Key Remnant there: reinforced, tied to the crime, at the centre of the region. Rows already pointing at a token are left alone.
Investigation.plannerCreated: Plan saved; {n} Key Remnant(s) placed on the map.

Vault.stowTooltip: Put this in your stash (you must be in the room)
Vault.takeTooltip: Take this back out (you must be in the room)
Vault.notHere: You have to be standing in your own room to reach your stash.
Vault.noBullets: Truth Bullets are what you know, not things in a drawer.
Vault.overflowed: Your hands were full, so {item} went into your stash. Your {category} limit is unchanged.
Vault.foundInStash: Hidden in this room, you find {item}.
Vault.stole: You take {item} out of {who}'s hiding place. They will notice it is gone.
Vault.manageIntro: What each room on this scene is: whose bedroom, whether its stash is hidden, what a search draws from, and what it is a good place to look for.
Vault.manageNote: A favoured category gives advantage to anyone searching here for it — medicine in the medic's office. A room with no table of its own falls through to the global pool, so half-finished setup is fine. One student, one bedroom.
Vault.noRooms: This scene has no room regions yet.
Vault.noneSet: No bedrooms have been assigned yet.
Vault.twoRooms: {name} cannot have two bedrooms ({a} and {b}). Pick one.
Vault.inspectNote: Take things out from Give / take items — a stashed item is an ordinary item on its owner's sheet.
Vault.rifleIntro: This is {who}'s stash, in {room}, and it is not hidden. Take one thing.
Vault.rifleNote: Free, and they will notice it is gone. A concealed stash needs a Search instead.
Vault.noOpenStashHere: There is no open stash in this room.
Vault.openStashNote: Not hidden. Anyone standing here can go through it.

Chapter.keepItems: Keep their inventory (not a killing-game death)
Chapter.deathNote: Everything they carried is destroyed, Truth Bullets included. That cannot be undone. The body stays on the map, but the dead stop counting as being in the room: they cannot witness, be handed anything, or block a murder happening there.
Chapter.vaultPending: Their stash was emptied with them — the count above includes anything put away.
Chapter.revived: {name} is no longer marked dead. Their destroyed inventory does not come back.
Chapter.deadPanelNote: The dead take no actions and spend no Hope. You keep your sheet and your voice at the table. Brought back as a Monocub, this panel becomes Move and Confusion.
Chapter.deadCannotAct: {name} is dead and cannot take actions.
Chapter.noRooms: This scene has no room regions to gather anyone into.
Chapter.bodyNote: Calls everyone to the scene and switches the phase to Investigation. First it offers you the doubtful Prep traces, so you can say which belong to this murder.
Chapter.bodyFound: A body has been found in {room}.
Chapter.bodyCalled: Everyone is called to the scene. The Investigation begins.
Chapter.bodyDone: {moved} moved to the scene, {promoted} trace(s) made permanent.
Chapter.promoteTitle: Which traces belong to this murder?
Chapter.promoteIntro: These Prep traces were left while somebody gathered tools. Most mean nothing. Tick the ones that belong to this killing.
Chapter.promoteNote: Ticked traces stop being doubtful: they survive the chapter-end sweep and count as evidence tied to the crime. Leave the rest and they go with everything else.
Chapter.endIntro: Chapter {chapter} is wrapping up. Tick what should happen.
Chapter.optReveal: Reveal what every Truth Bullet really is ({n} still unidentified)
Chapter.optRemnants: Clear Faint Remnants from the map ({n} would go)
Chapter.optSweep: Sweep Truth Bullets for the new session ({n} removed, {kept} Faint kept)
Chapter.endNote: Reveal at the end of the chapter; sweep at the start of the next session. Usually two different evenings, which is why they are two ticks. The sweep and the Remnant clear are both permanent.
Chapter.doneSweep: Swept {removed} Truth Bullet(s); {kept} Faint one(s) carried over.
Chapter.sweepReminder: New session — remember the Truth Bullet sweep. Nothing has been deleted yet.

Trial.presentTooltip: Put this in front of the whole trial
Trial.presentIntro: You are about to show {name} ({type}) to everyone. Only what you can see goes on the card. Never the GM's notes.
Trial.commentPlaceholder: e.g. This is why the timeline does not work.
Trial.presentNote: Present speaks in your turn. OBJECTION cuts somebody off — allowed only if you show a Truth Bullet, which is what this does.
Trial.notInTrial: Evidence is presented in a Class Trial. Outside one, share a copy instead.
Trial.failed: That could not be presented. Tell the GM.
Trial.logSummary: {total} presented this chapter, {objections} of them as an Objection.
Trial.logEmpty: Nothing has been presented this chapter yet.

Handover.shareTooltip: Share a copy with someone in this room
Handover.giveTooltip: Hand this to someone in this room
Handover.shareIntro: Who do you show {name} to? You are in {room}.
Handover.giveIntro: Who do you hand {name} to? You are in {room}.
Handover.shareNote: They get their own copy, you keep yours, and their copy is not bound by any failed analysis of yours. Costs no action.
Handover.giveNote: This leaves your inventory for good. Their carry limit still applies. No action.
Handover.nobodyHere: Nobody else in {room} to hand anything to.
Handover.tooFar: {name} is no longer in the room with you. Nothing changed hands.
Handover.theirHandsFull: {who} already carries the most {category} they can ({limit}).
Handover.failed: That handover did not go through. Tell the GM.
Handover.stuck: {who} handed over “{name}”, but their own copy could not be removed. Two exist now — delete one from their sheet.
Handover.alreadyHasIt: {who} already found that trace themselves. {name} would only be a duplicate.
Handover.receivedBulletFrom: {who} showed you {name}, and you have written down a copy.

Observe.anythingTitle: Observe — a question for the GM
Observe.requestPlaceholder: e.g. something to do with the body
Observe.declareNote: Sweeping the room finds the easiest trace in it; looking past the obvious finds the hardest. Naming what you are after, and asking the GM, both wait for the dice before you say what you meant.
Observe.requestPrompt: The dice are thrown. Now say what you were looking for. The GM matches it against the room without seeing your roll, so this makes nothing easier or harder.
Observe.requestConfirm: That is what I was after
Observe.requestSkipped: Nothing named — read as simply looking around.
Observe.sent: The GM is judging what you found.
Observe.noRuling: No GM settled what you were looking at. Your action is not spent.
Observe.failed: Nothing catches your eye. You take {stress} Stress.
Observe.critIdentified: You found it, and you know what kind of trace it is.
Observe.whichRemnant: Which Remnant are they closest to?
Observe.pickNote: Traces tied to the crime first, then easiest to hardest. They have already rolled, and you are not shown the number — pick what actually matches what they asked for.
Observe.pickConfirm: That is what they are looking at
Observe.describeIntro: {actor} found something in {room}. Name it as they would, and say what they see.
Observe.critPrompt: Critical — the category is identified for them, and they have earned a substantial hint.
Observe.rerollLost: A Reroll arrived for an Observe this browser has no record of — a reload, or another GM took over — so the declaration is lost. The dice are already rewritten and the player is owed a result: score the new number against the same trace by hand, and take back the Truth Bullet the first roll gave them if it no longer applies.

TruthBullet.name: Name — this is what the player sees
TruthBullet.shown: What the player is told it is
TruthBullet.shownAuto: By the rules — Key, Autopsy and Final arrive identified, the rest start Neutral
TruthBullet.shownReal: The real type — no analysis needed
TruthBullet.visibility: How hard the original was to spot
TruthBullet.visibilityTooltip: How visible the original Remnant was. This sets the difficulty of analysing it.
TruthBullet.faintField: Faint — survives the sweep at the start of the next session
TruthBullet.faintTooltip: Doubtful connection to the case. Survives into the next session and can be analysed again.
TruthBullet.lockedTooltip: You failed to analyse this one this chapter. Try again next chapter — or hand a copy to somebody else, who is not bound by your failure.
TruthBullet.playerTextPlaceholder: What the person who found it actually sees.
TruthBullet.gmNote: Note for the GM (never shown to the player)
TruthBullet.gmNotePlaceholder: What it really means for the case.
TruthBullet.secretNote: The real type and your note stay on the GM side. They never reach the player's item.
TruthBullet.whereToFind: It is in your inventory, under Truth Bullets.
TruthBullet.reallyTooltip: GM only — what this Truth Bullet actually is.
TruthBullet.autopsyHint: The state of the body — the time it was discovered, and the cause of death. Handed out at the start of every Investigation, never rolled for. Everyone is ticked; untick the victim.
TruthBullet.autopsyTextPlaceholder: Time of discovery, cause of death, and anything else the body shows.
TruthBullet.autopsyNobody: Nobody is ticked, so there is nobody to give it to.
TruthBullet.autopsyIssued: Autopsy Truth Bullet issued to {n} character(s).
TruthBullet.migratedTitle: Truth Bullets brought up to date
TruthBullet.migrated: {n} Truth Bullet(s) made before this version now carry a type, a visibility and a chapter. Their real type could not be recovered, so each is recorded as Neutral — correct the ones that matter from Give / take items.
TruthBullet.imported: Merged {n} Truth Bullet record(s) into the ledger.
TruthBullet.importFailed: That file is not a Truth Bullet ledger.

Inventory.overCap: {actor} is over the {category} limit ({held}/{limit}). Allowed — a GM granted it.
Inventory.full: You already carry the most {category} you can ({limit}).
Inventory.notCarried: (not picked up — that category is full)

Remnant.reinforced: That Remnant is reinforced and cannot be removed.
Remnant.noneHere: No Remnants on this scene yet.
Remnant.manageIntro: What survives the end of the chapter. Faint traces are swept away unless they are tied to the crime; reinforced ones the killer cannot remove at all.
Remnant.manageNote: Tick “tied to the crime” for anything the trial will need: a murder tool, a cleaning tool, or a trace left by the murder itself.
Remnant.noToken: {actor} has no token on any scene, so the trace could not be left. Tell the GM.
Remnant.noTokenGm: {actor} performed “{action}” with no token anywhere, so no Remnant was placed. Place one by hand if it matters.
Remnant.revealWarning: Remnants are your notes. Revealing this puts it on the map for everyone.
Remnant.searchNote: {actor} searched {room} for a {category} (rolled {total}) and came away with {item} — Tier {tier}.
Remnant.sabotageWorked: It worked: the project is frozen until {repair} is finished.
Remnant.sabotageFailed: It failed — the project is untouched, but the attempt left a trace.
Remnant.projectNote: {actor} worked on {project} in {room}, gaining {progress} progress, and rolled {total} to cover their tracks.

Rest.alreadyThisTimeOfDay: You have already taken a {kind} this time of day.
Rest.alreadyThisSession: You have already taken a {kind} this session.
Rest.alreadyThisTimeOfDayShort: already taken this time of day
Rest.wrongRoom: No {kind} in {room}. Rooms that allow it: {rooms}
Rest.noRooms: No room on this map is marked for a {kind} yet. The GM sets that up per scene.
Rest.manageIntro: Mark which rooms allow a Short Rest, and which are bedrooms allowing a Long Rest. Per scene, so every season's map can differ.
Rest.noRegions: This scene has no room regions. Draw them on the Regions layer first.

Calls.aimPlaceholderHope: e.g. Backing up the search of the library.
Calls.aimPlaceholderDespair: e.g. Slamming the kitchen door in their face.
Calls.noPool: This Monokuma has no Despair pool. Check the Despair bar.
Calls.nobodyHere: Nobody else is in this room.
Calls.noItems: Nobody carries anything that can be destroyed.
Calls.armed: {name} may now use {what} on their next roll.
Calls.sealed: {room} is sealed for this time of day.
Calls.effectFailed: {call} was paid for, but its effect could not be applied. See the console.
Calls.refunded: {call} did nothing, so the {cost} it cost has been returned.
Calls.silenced: {name} cannot spend Hope Calls until the clock moves.
Calls.silencedNotice: Monokuma has silenced you. No Hope Calls until this time of day ends.
Calls.chained: {name} is chained to {room} until the clock moves.
Calls.chainedNotice: Monokuma has chained you in place. You cannot leave this room until this time of day ends.
Calls.chainedBlocked: You are chained here until this time of day ends.
Calls.sealedBlocked: {room} is sealed for this time of day. Nobody gets in.
Calls.freeCritUsed: {name} takes the action and scores an automatic critical — no roll.
Calls.pendingTooltip: Waiting on your next roll: {what}. Spent the moment you roll.
Calls.noExperiences: This character has no experiences written down, so this Call has nothing to add.
Calls.armedTitle: A Call was made for you
Calls.armedForYou: Another student spent Hope on you: your next roll has {what}. It applies by itself.
Calls.newRulePrompt: Write the new rule. Every player sees it in chat, word for word.
Calls.newRulePlaceholder: e.g. From now on, nobody may enter the library alone.
Calls.newRuleNote: Twelve Despair buys a permanent change to the game. Make it count.
Calls.newRuleAnnounced: The new rule was announced to everyone.
Calls.noSuchRoom: There is no region called "{room}" on this scene.
Calls.progressRefused: {name} could not take the progress — it is already complete.

Monokuma.marked: {name} is now a Monokuma: no actions, no Hope, Despair Calls instead, and free movement.
Monokuma.panelIntro: Tick the actors that are Monokumas, then say whose Despair pool each draws on. Without this, two Monokumas share the pool of whichever Gamemaster is looking at the sheet.
Monokuma.panelNote: A Monokuma has no actions and no Hope: their sheet shows Despair Calls instead. The pool decides which Gamemaster pays for them.
Monokuma.sharedPool: {name}'s pool is shared by: {actors}. Each Monokuma should have their own.

Eclipse.title: Eclipse
Eclipse.announce: Lights out. Place your token — up to {n} connected rooms. Nobody sees anyone else until the Eclipse ends, and no actions or Calls until then.
Eclipse.yourMoves: {n} room crossings. You are in {room}. Drag your token — doors and gaps still apply.
Eclipse.noMovesLeft: Both Eclipse crossings are used. Your token has been put back.
Eclipse.notConnected: {to} is not connected to {from}. From here you can reach: {rooms}
Eclipse.actionsLocked: The Eclipse allows movement only. Actions and Calls return with the time of day.
Eclipse.endPrompt: End the Eclipse and begin the next time of day? Everyone has placed as follows:
Eclipse.endAndAdvance: End and start next time of day
Eclipse.announceFree: Lights out. Pick any room on the map and put your token there. Nobody sees anyone else until the Eclipse ends, and no actions or Calls until then.
Eclipse.yourMovesFree: Any room on the map. You are in {room}. Drag your token wherever you want to start.

Move.title: Move
Move.freeAvailable: Your free Move for this time of day is still there.
Move.freeSpent: Free Move used — the next room costs an action. You have {left}.
Move.wasFree: That was your free Move for this time of day.
Move.noBudget: No free Move and no actions left. Move your token back.
Move.notConnected: {to} is not connected to {from}. From here you can reach: {rooms}
Move.noBudgetLong: No free Move and no actions left — this crossing was not paid for. Move back, or ask the GM.

Project.heading: Projects
Project.title: Project
Project.choosePrompt: Start something new, or push a project that already exists?
Project.startPrompt: Describe the project for the GM: what you want to build or achieve, and where.
Project.startPlaceholder: e.g. Build a hidden compartment under the library floor.
Project.agreedWarning: This assumes you have already agreed the project with the GM. One you have not is one that gets deleted mid-session.
Project.startNote: Created at once and added to Projects. The GM is told, and can change the scale, the room, or remove it.
Project.startedOk: “{name}” created and added to Projects. The GM has been told.
Project.indirectMine: Indirect murder — kept secret, so only you and the GMs see it
Project.gmCanAdjust: Made by a player. Change the scale, room or secrecy from the Projects gear, or delete it.
Project.repaired: repaired. {name} can be worked on again.
Project.frozenNow: {name} is broken and frozen until {repair} is finished.
Project.alreadyFrozen: {name} is already broken and waiting on a repair.
Project.sabotageNotApplied: The roll succeeded, but no GM confirmed the damage in time. Tell your GM: {name} may not actually be broken.
Project.none: No projects yet. Start one first.
Project.wrongRoom: Nothing you can work on in {room}. Elsewhere: {names}
Project.aloneBonus: Nobody else is in the room, so the project gains +1 progress.
Project.createNote: Progress moves only when somebody uses Work on Project — never from attacks or rests. An indirect murder is made secret automatically.
Project.name: Name
Project.manageTooltip: Set which room each project belongs to, and who may see it
Project.manageIntro: A project can belong to a room. Only characters standing there can work on it or sabotage it.
Project.secretNote: Indirect murder projects are secret by default: only the killer and the GMs see them. Share to bring in a co-conspirator.
Project.changeImage: Click to change this project's image
Project.deleteNote: Tick Delete and Save to remove a project for good. Its progress and metadata do not come back.
Project.shareIntro: Let another player see this project. Players can bring in a co-conspirator; GMs can share with anyone.
Project.noPlayers: There are no players to share with.
Project.alreadyFull: {name} is already at {current}/{target}. No progress left to add.
Project.alreadyEmpty: {name} is already at 0. Nothing left to take away.
Project.noneHere: There is no project started in {room}.
Project.allSabotaged: Everything here is already broken or is itself a repair: {names}.
Project.someSabotaged: Not offered — already broken, or a repair project: {names}.
Project.editProgressNote: Progress is kept: this project is at {current}/{target}. Lowering the scale below what is earned clamps it.
Project.deleteConfirm: Delete "{name}"? Its progress goes with it.

RollDialog.locked: Not yours to choose. Advantage and experiences are Hope Calls — ask the GM.
RollDialog.diceFixed: Fixed at d12 by the rules.
RollDialog.advantageLocked: Advantage and disadvantage come from Calls, not from here.
RollDialog.pickOneExperience: Pick the one experience this roll relates to. Clicking another moves the choice.
RollDialog.experienceLocked: Using an experience is the Experience Hope Call — ask the GM to spend it.
RollDialog.bonusLocked: Situational bonuses are the GM's call.
RollDialog.modeLocked: Roll privacy is enforced by the module.
RollDialog.unlockedByCall: Unlocked by a Call you paid for.
RollDialog.freeCritArmed: Free Critical is armed. Both dice are forced to 12: 24, and a guaranteed critical.
RollDialog.forcedByCall: Set by a Call you paid for. It cannot be turned off.
RollDialog.forcedBySituation: Set by where you are and what you are looking for. It cannot be turned off.
RollDialog.lockedByCall: A Call has already decided this roll's modifier.

Bridge.criticalHint: Critical — this player is owed a substantial hint.
Bridge.noGm: No GM is connected, so that could not be sent.
Bridge.noAnswer: No GM answered the “{what}” request. Nothing was applied — try again once a GM is connected.

Tables.installed: Item tables ready: {created} created, {skipped} already existed.
Tables.allPresent: All {n} item tables already exist in this world.
Tables.rebuildNote: Rebuilding deletes them and builds them again from the module's own lists. Anything you edited by hand is lost.
Tables.someFailed: {n} item table(s) could not be created. See the console.
Tables.whereNote: The tables live in the Rollable Tables sidebar, in the “Danganronpa RPG” folder. Search reads them before falling back to the module's built-in lists.

Clock.searchTokensRestocked: Every room restocked with search tokens
Clock.woundedNote: Down to one action this time of day, all HP marked: {names}.

Panel.title: Danganronpa — GM Panel
Panel.gmOnly: Only a GM can open the panel.
Panel.nextIncident: An incident is running. Take it to the end before anything else.
Panel.nextEclipse: The Eclipse is open. Close it once everyone has placed.
Panel.nextNoFloor: The trial has no floor open — nobody can speak yet.
Panel.nextInvestigation: Investigation. Check what has been found and what is still out there.
Panel.nextStillActing: {n} student(s) still have actions to spend.
Panel.nextAllDone: Everyone has spent their actions. Move the clock on.
Panel.resetHint: Leave this off when you are only correcting a typo — refilling hands everyone a fresh set of actions.
Panel.alsoReset: Also refill actions and search tokens
Panel.noCharacters: No characters in this world yet.
Panel.voiceEavesdrop: Listen in on a room's voice
Panel.failed: That did not work. See the console.
Panel.faintNone: No Faint Remnants to clear — every trace on the map is reinforced or tied to the crime.
Panel.faintConfirm: Delete {n} Faint Remnant(s), across every scene?
Panel.faintConfirmNote: Reinforced traces and anything tied to the crime are left alone. The rest go for good.
Panel.whoIsWhatNote: Move a character between the three states. This only moves the flags — it does not destroy an inventory and does not bring one back. To kill somebody properly, use “A character dies”.

Character.notACharacter: That only works on a character.
Character.initTooltip: Not set up yet. Give them their starting resources: {hp} HP, {stress} Stress, {hope} Hope.
Character.initConfirm: Give {actor} their starting resources: {hp} HP, {stress} Stress and {hope} Hope?
Character.initNote: Until this is done the character counts as Wounded and in Breakdown: one action instead of two, and disadvantage on every roll.
Character.initNeeded: {n} character(s) still have no starting resources.
Character.initReady: Every character has their starting resources.
Character.startingItemNote: Agreed at character creation, tied to {ultimate}.
Character.startingItemMissing: No starting item named. Every student begins with one Tier 2 item tied to their Ultimate.

Advance.title: Level Up — {actor}
Advance.introMany: {reason} Choose {picks} improvements. You may take the same one more than once.

reason.reinforced: The Blackened walked out of a wrong vote.

Advance.newExperiencePlaceholder: a word or a sentence about who they are
Advance.noExperiences: This character has no experiences yet, so there is nothing to raise.
Advance.experienceNeedsName: A new experience needs a name. That choice was skipped.
Advance.nothingToApply: Nothing was selected, so nothing changed.
Advance.failed: The Level Up could not be saved. See the console.

Anonymity.notYours: Not your character. Sheets are private in this game.
Anonymity.forcedOnCreate: Default ownership was set to None to keep this sheet private.
Anonymity.blocked: Blocked: that would show “{actor}” to every player. Give the one player Owner instead.

audit.title: Sheet Anonymity Audit
audit.clean: Every character sheet is private. Nothing to fix.
audit.exposed: Visible to all players — fix these:
audit.assistants: Owned by an Assistant GM. Assistants read every sheet in the world, which breaks anonymity — drop them to Player:
audit.shared: Owned by more than one player:
audit.orphaned: No player owner assigned — here is who does have access:

Errors.wrongSystem: The Danganronpa RPG module needs the Daggerheart system (Foundryborne). Found: {found}.
Errors.oldSystem: Written against Daggerheart {required} or newer. Found {found} — some features may misbehave.

Reroll.title: Reroll
Reroll.nothingToReroll: You have not rolled anything, so there is nothing to take back.
Reroll.notARoll: Your last message carries no dice.
Reroll.failed: The reroll could not be applied. See the console.
Reroll.despairGained: The new result is a Despair result: {name} gains 1 Despair.
Reroll.despairReturned: The old result was a Despair result: 1 Despair is returned to {name}.
Reroll.critHopeGained: The new result is a critical: you gain the second point of Hope a crit is worth.
Reroll.critHopeReturned: The old result was a critical: the second point of Hope it paid is taken back.
Reroll.progressAdjusted: {name}: progress from this action changed from {was} to {now}.
Reroll.leftovers: Anything the first roll already produced — an item drawn, a trace left — stays put. Ask the GM to remove it if the new result does not justify it.
Reroll.noReplay: Nothing but the dice to take back: this roll left no lasting effect.
Reroll.replayFailed: The dice were rerolled, but the action could not be replayed. Tell the GM what the first roll had already done.
Reroll.observeReplayed: The same trace goes back to the GM with the new roll. They will say what you find this time.
Reroll.analyzeReplayed: The same Truth Bullet is analysed again with the new roll. Any lock the first attempt left is lifted first.
Reroll.crisisReplayed: The crisis action is taken back and made again with the new roll — the damage, the trace and any hindrance go with it. The turn is not spent twice.
Reroll.cleanupReplayed: The clean-up is taken back and attempted again. The trace comes back, anything the botched wipe left is removed, and the Stress is refunded first.
Reroll.itemTakenBack: {item} is taken back out of your inventory.
Reroll.itemStuck: {item} could not be removed automatically — ask the GM to take it.
Reroll.tokenKept: The room's search token stays spent — the room was searched either way.
Reroll.remnantRetuned: The trace you left is now {visibility}.
Reroll.remnantLeft: The new result leaves a trace behind: {visibility}.
Reroll.remnantRemoved: The trace the first roll left is removed.
Reroll.remnantManual: The trace the first roll left cannot be adjusted from here — ask the GM to re-rate it.
Reroll.sabotageUndone: The first attempt is undone: the target is unfrozen and its repair project removed.
Reroll.sabotageRedone: {name} breaks again — the repair now needs {n} progress.
Reroll.sabotageNowFails: The new result fails: the target is left working.
Reroll.actionTakenBack: The critical is gone, so the action it returned is spent again.
Reroll.actionOwed: The critical is gone, but the action it returned is already used. You owe one.
Reroll.gmReasked: The GM has been asked to rule again on the new result.
Reroll.rulingVoid: Rerolled: {old} no longer stands, the result is now {new}. Please rule again.

Messenger.rosterEmpty: No players in this world yet.
Messenger.onlyOwnThread: You can only open your own conversation.
Messenger.notAPlayer: Messenger threads exist for players, not for the GM team.

Voice.notActive: LiveKit AVClient is not installed, not active, or not connected.
Voice.eavesdropFailed: Could not join that room's voice channel. See the console.
Voice.noRooms: No mapped rooms on that scene yet.
Voice.eavesdropPrompt: Join a room's voice channel as a muted listener. Leave to return to the main room.
Voice.onScene: Rooms on {scene} — the scene your own Monokuma is standing on, or the one you are viewing.
Voice.needsAvclient: Regional voice is on, but LiveKit AVClient is not active.
Voice.avDisabled: Regional voice is on, but Audio/Video is off for this world. Turn it on in Configure Settings.
Voice.resetDone: {n} player(s) sent back to the main voice room.
Voice.resetRefused: Nothing to reset: regional voice is off, LiveKit is inactive, or another GM's client is running it.

drpgBreakdown.name: Breakdown
drpgBreakdown.description: Every point of Stress is marked. Disadvantage on every roll.

drpgWounded.name: Wounded
drpgWounded.description: Every point of HP is marked. One action fewer per time of day.

Rules.sheetIntro: Monokuma's standing rules. They apply to everyone, all the time, until he says otherwise.
Rules.manageIntro: Every standing rule, in the order they were introduced. Edit the wording in place, tick to revoke, or add one at the bottom.
Rules.manageNote: Rules bought with the New Rule Despair Call land here by themselves. Everything here shows on every character sheet.
Rules.recorded: Added to the killing game's standing rules.

Motive.title: Motive
Motive.withdrawn: The motive is withdrawn. Nothing hanging over you — for now.
Motive.untilChapterEnd: In force until the end of this chapter.

Safeword.title: Safeword
Safeword.tooltip: Stop the scene. No reason needed, and nobody will ask for one.
Safeword.confirmNote: The game pauses, every GM is told, and everyone sees that the scene has stopped. You do not have to justify it, now or later.
Safeword.announced: Somebody used the safeword. Play stops here. A GM will pick this up, and the scene resumes from a point everyone agrees on.
Safeword.gmNote: {who} used it, in {room}. Nobody else has been told who — the table only knows the scene stopped.
Safeword.failed: The safeword could not be sent. Say it out loud and tag a GM.

Note.intro: Your plans for the session, for the GMs. They read it before every session and steer around it — the first four questions are boundaries, not a dare. Nothing has changed? Write “No changes” and you are done.
Note.gmIntro: This player's pre-session note. You can edit it — they will see what you wrote.
Note.saveFailed: The note could not be saved. See the console.
Note.q1: Am I planning to kill? How? Direct or indirect, and how I avoid getting caught.
Note.q2: Am I open to the possibility of dying?
Note.q3: Do I consent to my character being tortured?
Note.q4: Am I open to a romance involving my character?
Note.q6: How do I plan to play? What are my goals?
Note.q7: I am planning to try: … (complex, game-changing projects)

Summary.title: The time of day is over
